traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Hydrophyllaceae, which takes in Hydroleaceae: leaves alternate or opposite; leaves simple or compound; compound leaves usually pinnate, rarely palmate; veins usually pinnate, rarely palmate; stipules absent; leaf rosettes basal or none; plants hermaphrodite; ovary usually superior, sometimes half inferior; floral cup absent; joined corolla rotate, campanulate or funnelform; stems usually herbaceous, sometimes woody; flowers usually in cymes, rarely solitary; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule; parts of each whorl 5; stamens (4-) 5 (-10); carpels 2. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
